what_its_for: Ambrisentan is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the blood vessels that go from your heart to your lungs. It helps relax and widen these blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard, making it easier for you to breathe and exercise.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember. If you have trouble swallowing it, talk to your doctor or pharmacist before changing how you take it.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg once daily if needed. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store ambrisentan at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of unused or expired tablets safely — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Do not take cyclosporine (a medicine used after organ transplants) while on ambrisentan, as it can raise your ambrisentan levels dangerously. Avoid becoming pregnant — ambrisentan causes serious birth defects and must never be used during pregnancy. Women who can become pregnant must use two reliable forms of birth control. Do not donate blood while taking this medication. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice as it may affect how this medicine works. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: swelling of your hands, feet, ankles, or legs; shortness of breath that gets worse; rapid weight gain (more than 2 pounds in a day); signs of liver problems such as nausea, stomach pain, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes; feeling very tired or weak; low red blood cell count (anemia) symptoms like dizziness, unusual tiredness, or pale skin; or if you think you might be pregnant. Call 911 or go to the emergency room if you have severe difficulty breathing or chest pain.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some improvement in your ability to exercise and breathe within the first few weeks of treatment. However, it may take several weeks to months to feel the full benefit of this medicine. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you feel well, because stopping suddenly can make your condition worse.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine must NOT be used during pregnancy. It causes severe birth defects. Women who can become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before starting, every month during treatment, and one month after stopping. Two effective forms of birth control must be used at the same time. This drug is part of a restricted program called the Ambrisentan REMS Program. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Liver disease: This medicine is not recommended if you have moderate to severe liver problems. Tell your doctor about any liver conditions before starting. Kidney disease: Usually no dose adjustment is needed for kidney problems, but always inform your doctor. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been fully established — use only as directed by a specialist.
